patches.old_string: Non-discriminating. Both models predict continued SAA weakening. The dome extrapolates station decay rates; the globe derives decay from core-mantle boundary dynamics. Neither model's specific nT threshold can distinguish them — they are both predicting the same direction from the same data. patches.new_string:
Non-discriminating. Both models predict continued SAA weakening. The dome extrapolates station decay rates; the globe derives decay from core-mantle boundary dynamics. Neither model's specific nT threshold can distinguish them — they are both predicting the same direction from the same data. The only difference is mechanism: the dome attributes decay to "aetheric field stress at the ovoid shoulder," while the globe attributes it to reversed flux patches at the core-mantle boundary. A discriminating test would require the two mechanisms to predict different decay rates or trajectories — but the dome's prediction is derived from the globe's own observational data (CHAOS-7), so they cannot diverge.

When the dome did make a discriminating SAA claim, it failed — and was never scored. The field-strength prediction above is non-discriminating, but the dome registered exactly one SAA claim that genuinely diverged from standard physics: PRED-073, predicting the SAA western cell would drift ≥0.3° further westward in a single month (April→May 2026), driven by "toroidal aetheric return flow" (data/predictions.json:PRED-073). Credit where due: it was genuinely prospective — hash-committed before the window, with an explicit falsification rule ("drifts <0.1° westward or reverses"). But annualized, ≥0.3°/month is ~3.65°/yr — roughly 12–13× the observed western-cell rate of 0.282 ± 0.030°/yr derived from the same CHAOS-7 source the dome itself cites (Finlay et al., 2020). Standard secular variation implies ~0.024° of drift over that month — an order of magnitude below the dome's threshold, squarely inside its own falsification criterion. (One honest caveat: no published CHAOS release covers April–May 2026 — the dome cited an already-deprecated verification source at registration — so the falsified verdict rests on the well-constrained secular rate rather than a direct post-window measurement.) The window closed 2026-05-31; the dome posted no result, and the entry still sits as pending on its own predictions page (see Section 6.15, the silent-ignore cohort). The pattern completes this test's verdict: where the dome's SAA predictions are derived from globe data, they are safe and non-discriminating; the one time an SAA claim diverged from the standard rate, it failed — and the dome's scoreboard never recorded the miss.
